sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Enterprise AI Adoption: 59% Spend $1M+, 29% See ROI [2026] - tech-insider.org

Canadian businesses more than tripled their use of artificial intelligence in two years, moving from 6.1% adoption in the second quarter of 2024 to 19.2% by the same period in 2026, according to Statistics Canada.
Globally the pattern looks even sharper: 59% of organizations now spend at least $1 million a year on AI, based on a WRITER-commissioned survey of 2,400 executives and employees published in 2026.

The Productivity Paradox: 5x Personal Gains, 29% Company ROI Canada vs. the United States: A Smaller, Slower ROI Curve Market Impact: What the ROI Gap Means for Vendors and Buyers Competitive Comparison: How OpenAI, Microsoft, Google and Anthropic Are Responding What Comes Next: 5 Predictions for Enterprise AI Spending That gap between AI spending and AI payoff has become the defining budget fight inside technology departments this year.

Workplace Intelligence polled 2,400 people on WRITER’s behalf: 1,200 C-suite executives and 1,200 employees at companies ranging from 100 to more than 10,000 workers, spread across nearly 30 industries in the United States, United Kingdom, Ireland, the Benelux region, France, and Germany.
Fifty-nine percent of companies now invest $1 million or more annually in AI technology.

And in a finding that should worry any finance team, 54% of C-suite respondents said AI adoption is tearing their company apart internally, the product of fights over budget ownership, tool sprawl, and who decides which model powers which workflow.
The same WRITER research found that 67% of executives believe their company has already suffered a data breach tied to unapproved, employee-installed AI tools, a pattern often called shadow AI.
Seventy-nine percent of organizations now call AI a strategic priority, up from 74% in the first quarter, and 22% classify AI as simply part of everyday work, up from 13% the quarter before.
Average AI spending among surveyed organizations reached $188 million.
Despite that scale of investment, just 7% of organizations told KPMG they had established measurable ROI on their AI spending.

Twenty-four percent of organizations say they struggle specifically with managing usage-based AI costs, and 49% have already delayed or scaled back an AI initiative after its cost exceeded its measured value.
Companies with 100 or more employees report 27.8% adoption, compared with 19.9% among the smallest businesses.
Urban firms sit at 21.0% adoption versus 9.9% in rural areas.
Information and cultural industries lead the country at 42.3% adoption, followed by finance and insurance at 40.4% and professional, scientific, and technical services at 32.4%.

Statistics Canada also found that 44.4% of businesses using AI made training or staffing changes as a direct result, evidence that adoption is reshaping headcount decisions well before most companies have settled the ROI question.
For more on the policy side of that push, see our coverage of Canada’s $200 billion national AI strategy and how it aims to accelerate adoption in the sectors currently lagging.
Sixty-nine percent of Canadian firms report partial or full AI integration, compared with 89% in the United States.
On returns, 43% of Canadian companies say their AI investments have exceeded ROI expectations, against 57% of American companies.
On spending intentions, only 41% of Canadian firms plan to invest $1 million or more in AI this fiscal year, versus 62% south of the border.

records.evidence:
In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate dropped 41 percent compared with 2024, though the region still posted the highest rate of any market DoubleVerify tracks, at 0.6 percent, driven mainly by the United States.
EMEA marketers instead prioritized the ability to review or approve AI-generated creatives, at 38 percent, ahead of data-privacy safeguards.
The company derives its wasted-spend estimates by multiplying total violations by an assumed cost per mille of 3 dollars, a figure the report applies uniformly across markets despite considerable variation in actual media pricing between, for instance, the United States and other markets in the same region.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.

Reach out via luis@ppc.land LinkedIn DoubleVerify today released regional editions of its 2026 Global Insights report, "Media Quality in the Age of AI," reporting that fraud and invalid traffic violation rates fell 41 percent year over year in North America and 45 percent in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, while artificial intelligence bots generated up to ten times more clicks than humans in some unprotected ad campaigns.

In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate dropped 41 percent compared with 2024, though the region still posted the highest rate of any market DoubleVerify tracks, at 0.6 percent, driven mainly by the United States.
The Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate fell 45 percent year over year, continuing what DoubleVerify describes as the world's lowest regional rate for the metric.
Non-human data center traffic, the most prevalent fraud type in the region, dropped 54 percent.

Unprotected campaigns, meaning those without DoubleVerify's pre-bid or post-bid safeguards, recorded a fraud violation rate of 2.8 percent globally, compared with 0.6 percent for protected campaigns, a difference the report expresses as 384 percent.

That comparison echoes the structure of DoubleVerify's own Q1 2026 quarterly benchmarks report , which similarly found fraud and SIVT violations falling 24 percent year over year to 0.5 percent globally in that earlier dataset, alongside a rising out-of-geo violation rate that ran counter to the broader trend.

In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate on desktop stood at 0.9 percent, against 0.8 percent on mobile app and 0.5 percent on mobile web; desktop showed the steepest year-over-year reduction, at 48 percent.

In EMEA, the pattern reversed: mobile app recorded the largest improvement, falling 51 percent to reach a 0.4 percent violation rate, while desktop, at 0.8 percent, improved by 44 percent and mobile web, at 0.2 percent, improved by 49 percent.

The lab found that in unprotected media, AI bots generated 15 percent of clicks across the campaigns studied, and that in some individual studies, a monitored ad click was ten times more likely to come from a bot than from a human.

A State of Click Fraud Report published by Lunio in July 2026 found that 75.6 percent of surveyed marketers estimated losing more than 5 percent of their monthly performance budget to invalid traffic, while only 5.3 percent used a dedicated prevention platform.

North America's Brand Suitability Violation Rate fell to 4.1 percent, a 10 percent year-over-year reduction and the lowest of any region DoubleVerify tracks; the figure has now declined for three consecutive years, from 5.4 percent in 2023 to 4.6 percent in 2024 and 4.1 percent in 2025.

Within North America, the United States recorded a 4 percent violation rate against Canada's 8 percent, though Canada's figure dropped 11 percent year over year compared with a 9 percent reduction in the United States.
EMEA's rate fell only 2 percent, to 6.9 percent, and the region continued to underperform the 4.8 percent global benchmark.

The regional average obscured wide variation by market: France's violation rate dropped sharply, to 4 percent, below the global benchmark, while rates in Italy and Turkey rose year over year, and Eastern Europe recorded the highest subregional rate at 9.9 percent, even as that figure itself fell 14 percent from the prior year.
Globally, unprotected campaigns recorded a 13.8 percent brand suitability violation rate against 4.8 percent for protected campaigns, a gap DoubleVerify expresses as 189 percent.

The report's Vodafone Germany case study found that after implementing DoubleVerify's Authentic Brand Suitability product, the telecommunications company reduced media waste by 79 percent and its block rate by 72 percent, alongside CPM and quality-adjusted CPM reductions of 4 percent and 10 percent respectively.

Similar deployment findings for Vodafone in EMEA news environments appeared in an earlier PPC Land report from July 2025, which found the company had reduced block rates by 41 percent and keyword violations by 48 percent year over year, redirecting the resulting savings into additional purchases of news publisher inventory.
DoubleVerify says its AI SlopStopper tool blocked or monitored more than 500 million impressions across both regions in the first half of 2026 combined.

North American marketers reported far greater reluctance than their global counterparts about using AI to build ad copy and creatives: 63 percent said they were somewhat to very concerned, against a 48 percent global figure.
EMEA marketers showed the opposite pattern, expressing less concern than the global average, at 43 percent against 45 percent globally.

North American marketers proved the most wary of any group in either report about serving ads inside AI platforms, with 63 percent describing themselves as somewhat to very concerned, against a 50 percent global average; EMEA marketers were closer to that global figure, at 47 percent.

Consumer reactions in North America followed a similar pattern, with only the single scenario of "the ad is highly relevant to the chat" producing more positive than negative sentiment, at 31 percent positive against 19 percent negative.
Ads appearing alongside chats the report characterizes as negative or sad drew 34 percent negative sentiment in North America, the least favorable result recorded for any chat scenario tested.
North American marketers ranked transparent reporting on where ads are served and reliable measurement and attribution of ad performance as their top two requirements, both at 39 percent.
EMEA marketers instead prioritized the ability to review or approve AI-generated creatives, at 38 percent, ahead of data-privacy safeguards.

North America's overall viewable rate rose 4 percent year over year; video viewability in the United States specifically climbed 10 percent to reach 88 percent, while Canada's video rate rose a more modest 4 percent to 84 percent.

EMEA video viewability rose only 1 percent regionally, to 84 percent, still trailing the 87 percent global benchmark, though France recorded the sharpest single-market improvement in display viewability, up 8 percent to 67 percent.
July 16, 2025 - Vodafone reports a 10 percent increase in accessible news publisher inventory after adopting DoubleVerify's AI-powered brand suitability tools, cutting block rates 41 percent.
July 19, 2025 - IAS identifies AI-generated slop sites as a major ad quality threat , finding quality inventory delivers 91 percent higher conversion rates.

July 7, 2026 - DoubleVerify's Q1 2026 quarterly benchmarks show fraud falling 24 percent year over year globally, alongside a rising out-of-geo violation rate.

Rambus（RMBS）delivered a landmark quarter, shattering the $200 million revenue ceiling for the first time in its history.

The chip interface and IP specialist reported second-quarter revenue of $207.4 million, a 20% jump from a year ago and 15% higher than the previous quarter, driven by an insatiable appetite for faster memory in AI data centers and the accelerating shift to DDR5 technology.
Product revenue, the company's main growth engine, surged 22% year-over-year to $99.2 million.
Non-GAAP net income climbed to $84.4 million, translating to earnings of $0.77 per share, a 24% improvement over the prior-year period.
Cash generation remained robust, with operating cash flow of $61 million and free cash flow of $49 million.
Rambus ended the quarter with a fortified balance sheet, holding $825 million in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities.
In a deliberate move to navigate persistent supply chain tightness, Rambus increased its inventory by $16 million during the quarter.
The Silicon IP business remains a steady growth pillar, with management projecting an annual expansion rate of 10% to 15%.

For the third quarter, Rambus guided for revenue between $210 million and $216 million, with product revenue expected to land between $110 million and $116 million, representing a sequential increase of roughly 14% at the midpoint.
Non-GAAP earnings per share are forecast in the range of $0.75 to $0.82.
Rambus maintained its long-term product gross margin target of 60% to 65%, though quarterly fluctuations are expected due to product mix shifts and ongoing supply constraints.

records.evidence:
The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.
The report, The Next Growth Market: Inside the $675 Billion Consumer Opportunity , examines the purchasing power of working-age adults with disabilities (aged 16–64) and argues that businesses across every sector stand to benefit by designing products, services and customer experiences that better meet the needs of disabled consumers.
As previously reported, research has estimated the global disability market to be worth US$13 trillion in annual spending power , making it one of the world’s largest consumer segments.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Disability Consumer Market Hits $675 Billion, Creating Growth Opportunity for Businesses

New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world’s largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.

The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.

The report, The Next Growth Market: Inside the $675 Billion Consumer Opportunity , examines the purchasing power of working-age adults with disabilities (aged 16–64) and argues that businesses across every sector stand to benefit by designing products, services and customer experiences that better meet the needs of disabled consumers.
As previously reported, research has estimated the global disability market to be worth US$13 trillion in annual spending power , making it one of the world’s largest consumer segments.
The report estimates that the disability consumer market is now worth $675 billion, equivalent in size to the global beauty and cosmetics industry.
Annual discretionary income across the disability community has reached $107 billion.
Approximately 10% of working-age people with disabilities have an average $40,000 in discretionary spending power each year.
Those consumers have an average pre-tax income of $135,805, reflecting a growing segment with significant purchasing power.

“The opportunity presented by the $675 billion disability consumer market is enormous, especially for businesses that develop accessible products, emerge as the brand of choice by capturing everyday consumer dollars and include people with disabilities in their go-to-market strategies.”
The study found that: Average disposable income for people with disabilities is approximately $40,000 per year.
Average disposable income for people without disabilities is around $68,000 annually.

“If the momentum achieved over the past 10 years is any indication of what the future holds, then we can project with confidence that the favourable trends identified in our research will bear brighter tomorrows for the disability community, businesses at large and the US economy overall.”

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Disposable Gloves Market Size to Hit USD 24.92 Bn by 2035
The global disposable gloves market was valued at USD 11.21 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 24.92 billion by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 8.32% from 2026 to 2035.

The global disposable gloves market size is calculated at USD 11.21 billion in 2025 and is predicted to increase from USD 12.15 billion in 2026 to approximately USD 24.92 billion by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 8.32% from 2026 to 2035.
North America dominated the global disposable gloves market with the largest market share of 37.41% in 2025.
As per the worldwide disposable gloves import data recorded between July 2024 and June 2025, the buyers have globally imported 1,288 shipments of Disposable gloves.
Such shipments were being helped by 1,28 explorers and bought by 1,984 official worldwide buyers, which has shown a 33% increase as compared to the last year.

(Source: https://www.volza.com ) Malaysia has shipped 10,776 shipments, followed by China with 7,076 shipments and Vietnam with 5,254 shipments, which have ranked as the biggest worldwide disposable gloves exporters.

records.evidence:
Valid responses totaled 10,000 for the screening survey and 3,300 for the main survey.
Its first survey, titled "Consumer AI Usage Survey 2026.7," examined how AI is being used in purchasing behavior and decision-making.
Dentsu Digital said the findings show AI use is spreading in awareness, comparison and post-purchase phases, while people still account for a higher share of decision-making at the final stage.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Dentsu Digital survey finds 57% use AI for travel planning

Dentsu Digital launches with AI Lab and publishes a July 2026 survey on consumer AI use in purchasing About one in three private AI users consult AI before purchases, with travel and financial categories above 50% AI use is strongest in awareness, comparison and post-purchase stages, while final buying decisions remain more human-led Dentsu Digital said on July 23 that about one in three consumers who use artificial intelligence in their private lives had consulted AI about purchases made within the past six months, releasing the first findings from a new in-house research unit focused on consumer behavior in the AI era.

The ratio was highest in higher-involvement categories where consumers tend to compare options more closely, with 57% in travel planning and accommodation bookings and 56% in financial products and insurance.

Across product categories, 2% to 3% of respondents said they adopted AI responses as-is for their final decision, indicating that some consumers are beginning to leave the ultimate purchase choice to AI.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: [The 'Next' of Generative AI] The '$50 Trillion Market' Jensen Huang Spoke Of. How Individual Investors Can Prepare to Ride a Once-in-a-Decade Wave｜日本個別株デューデリジェンスセンター
He has been repeatedly mentioning a figure of '$50 trillion,' a scale that is hard to believe.

In this article, I will carefully break down what the next theme Huang calls 'Physical AI' means, analyze the components of that $50 trillion figure, and explain how individual investors should approach this wave, which is being called a 'once-in-a-decade' opportunity.
The figure of $50 trillion is so massive that it feels unreal.
In Japanese yen, that is well over 7,000 trillion yen.
Huang described this as 'the first $50 trillion industry that the technology sector can reach.'
What is important is that this $50 trillion is not a 'market available right now.'
So, where is the main battlefield for this $50 trillion?
Waymo currently provides about 500,000 paid rides per week in about 10 U.S. cities, and its fleet of about 3,000 vehicles travels about 4 million miles autonomously per week.
It aims to reach 1 million rides per week by the end of 2026, and its corporate value has reached approximately $126 billion.
At CES, Boston Dynamics announced that it would ship its mass-produced Atlas within 2026, and it was reported that South Korea's Hyundai Motor plans to produce 30,000 units annually by 2028.

values.label: 도입률

records.evidence:
At the same time, higher costs and improving durability are extending replacement cycles from approximately 3.5 to 4 years, making upgrade decisions more deliberate.
With 45% willing to pay more for performance and 57% for camera, users are prioritising reliability and consistency .
As the category matures, this evolution reflects a transition from rapid adoption to more considered, need-based buying behaviour, with consumers increasingly prioritising how devices fit into their everyday usage across work, entertainment and content creation.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: AI, Performance and Affordability Emerge as Key Drivers of Smartphone Buying in India: Counterpoint Research X Flipkart Report ● AI is becoming a key purchase driver, with nearly 9 in 10 users influenced by AI features ● Performance, camera capabilities and reliability continue to shape smartphone preferences across segments ● Longer replacement cycles and rising EMI adoption reflect more deliberate, value-driven buying behaviour April 29, 2026: Flipkart, India’s homegrown e-commerce marketplace, in collaboration with Counterpoint Research, unveiled the Smartphone Insights Report 2026 at Flipkart - India’s Favourite Smartphone Awards, attended by over 400 creators, brands and industry partners.

BCG Report Projects Gaming Industry Revenues Will Hit $350 Billion by 2030 Cloud Gaming Revenue Will Reach $18.3 Billion by 2030, Up 57% from 2023 40% of Gamers Are Consuming More User-Generated Content Than Last Year BOSTON —The gaming industry is emerging from its post-pandemic slowdown, with global gaming revenue projected to grow by 6% from 2026 to 2030 and reach $350 billion by 2030.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: BCG Report Projects Gaming Industry Revenues Will Hit $350 Billion by 2030 Cloud Gaming Revenue Will Reach $18.3 Billion by 2030, Up 57% from 2023 40% of Gamers Are Consuming More User-Generated Content Than Last Year BOSTON —The gaming industry is emerging from its post-pandemic slowdown, with global gaming revenue projected to grow by 6% from 2026 to 2030 and reach $350 billion by 2030.
A new survey of approximately 3,000 gamers found that 55% of them increased their playing time during the past six months.
UGC has emerged as a rapidly growing creator economy, with payouts that will reach $1.5 billion in 2025 from two games alone.
More than 40% of survey respondents said that they’re consuming more UGC this year than last year, but only 10% to 15% have created content themselves.
Although 60% of respondents said they had tried cloud gaming, and 80% reported a positive experience, only 27% of gamers said they are regular or heavy users of cloud gaming.
Still, cloud gaming revenues are set to grow from around $1.4 billion in 2025 to $18.3 billion in 2030, and the number of users will surpass 50 million.
BCG’s report estimates that mobile in-app purchases in 2025 will approach $130 billion, nearly half of global industry revenue.

records.evidence:
Americans are much more concerned than excited about the increased use of AI in daily life, with a majority saying they want more control over how AI is used in their lives.
Americans on the risks, benefits of AI – in their own words Pew Research Center conducted this study to understand Americans’ views of artificial intelligence (AI) and its potential impact on people and society.
Building on our larger body of work tracking public opinion about AI’s societal impact, this study examines how Americans view AI’s effect on human abilities, as well as broader questions about AI’s impact on society.
